seo.title: Canberra homeless help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified shelter, food, health, safety, legal and social support for people experiencing homelessness in Canberra.

page.heading: CANBERRA - HOMELESS HELP
page.urgent: Immediate danger or medical emergency: 000. No safe place to sleep: FIRST Canberra 1800 176 468.
page.notice: Information and availability can change. Call before travelling when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, meal, appointment, benefit, treatment or job.
page.intro: If you have nowhere safe to sleep, contact FIRST Canberra before going to an accommodation service. It is the ACT central intake service and can assess your situation and connect you with available housing and support. During the day, the Early Morning Centre is a practical place for food, showers, phone access and referrals.
page.footer: Main sources: ACT Government, Canberra Health Services, Early Morning Centre, Legal Aid ACT, Services Australia, Domestic Violence Crisis Service and the listed organisations.

entries.title: FIRST Canberra
entries.description: ACT central intake and referral service for people who are homeless or at risk. Staff assess needs, explain housing options and connect people with crisis accommodation and support. A placement depends on assessment and availability.
entries.hours: Monday to Friday 8:00am-6:00pm; Saturday and Sunday 12:30pm-5:00pm
entries.how_to_access: Call first. Do not travel to a shelter expecting a bed without an assessment.

entries.title: Lifeline Canberra
entries.description: Confidential crisis support for anyone who feels overwhelmed or unsafe. Call 13 11 14; call 000 if there is immediate danger.
entries.how_to_access: Call 13 11 14 or use the online crisis chat.

entries.title: FIRST Canberra housing assessment
entries.description: The official first point of contact for crisis accommodation and homelessness support in the ACT. FIRST can refer adults, families and young people to the service that matches their circumstances.
entries.hours: Monday to Friday 8:00am-6:00pm; Saturday and Sunday 12:30pm-5:00pm
entries.how_to_access: Call for assessment. Accommodation is not guaranteed and depends on urgency, eligibility and available places.

entries.title: Early Morning Centre
entries.description: Free breakfast, lunches, tea, coffee and emergency food packs. The centre also provides showers, toilets, lockers, phone, computers, internet, health visits and accommodation referrals. Everyone is welcome; no eligibility conditions are published.
entries.hours: Breakfast Monday-Friday 7:30am-8:30am; community hub weekdays 9:00am-2:00pm and weekends 9:00am-1:00pm

entries.title: Vinnies Roadhouse
entries.description: Evening meal and drop-in support in central Canberra. The ACT Government and Early Morning Centre resource list identify the Roadhouse as a local meal service.
entries.address: Griffin Centre, 20 Genge Street, Canberra City ACT
entries.hours: Dinner Saturday to Thursday; confirm current serving time
entries.how_to_access: Check the current timetable before travelling.

entries.title: St John's Care
entries.description: Community pantry and practical assistance, including food and clothing. The service operates from the St John's Church precinct and works with people facing financial hardship.
entries.how_to_access: Call before visiting and ask what identification or referral is needed.

entries.title: Early Morning Centre facilities
entries.description: Free toilets and showers, with access to lockers, phone, computers and internet. The centre also hosts visiting support and health services.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in during community hub hours.

entries.title: St John's Care clothing support
entries.description: Practical help for people in hardship, including clothing and a community pantry. Availability changes with donations.
entries.how_to_access: Call and ask what is available and whether an appointment is required.

entries.title: Canberra Health Services Walk-in Centres
entries.description: Free treatment by nurses for non-life-threatening injuries and illness. No appointment is needed. For a life-threatening emergency call 000 or go to an emergency department.
entries.hours: Daily; check the official page for locations and current hours
entries.how_to_access: Walk in. Medicare cards are not required for the nurse-led service.

entries.title: Health services at the Early Morning Centre
entries.description: Visiting health care, alcohol and drug counselling and referrals are available through the community hub. The exact visiting timetable changes.
entries.how_to_access: Ask staff which health service is visiting that day.

entries.title: Access Mental Health
entries.description: ACT entry point for public mental health assessment, information and referral. Call 000 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Early Morning Centre phone and internet
entries.description: Guests can use a phone, computers and internet while the community hub is open.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in and ask staff to use the facilities.

entries.title: Services Australia support when homeless
entries.description: Information about Centrelink payments, urgent payments, social workers and replacing Medicare cards. A Services Australia social worker can help connect you with other supports.
entries.how_to_access: Call or visit a service centre. Ask to speak with a social worker if you need additional support.

entries.title: Workforce Australia
entries.description: Government employment service with job search, provider support and help preparing for work. Eligibility for provider services depends on circumstances.
entries.how_to_access: Use the website or ask Services Australia whether you can be referred to a provider.

entries.title: Legal Aid ACT
entries.description: Free legal information and, for eligible people, legal advice or representation. Services cover areas including housing, family violence, family law and criminal law.
entries.how_to_access: Call the Legal Aid Helpline before visiting where possible.

entries.title: Domestic Violence Crisis Service ACT
entries.description: Confidential crisis intervention, safety planning and support for people affected by domestic or family violence in the ACT.
entries.how_to_access: Call the crisis line. Call 000 if there is immediate danger.

entries.title: Pets in the Park at the Early Morning Centre
entries.description: Periodic veterinary clinics for pets belonging to eligible guests. A written referral is required and Early Morning Centre staff can issue it.
entries.how_to_access: Visit or call the Early Morning Centre to ask for a referral and the next clinic date.
